name: Per-Screen Workspaces
description:
Independent workspaces on every monitor, like macOS Spaces.

By default GNOME has one active workspace shared by all screens: switching on one screen switches them all. With Per-Screen Workspaces, each monitor has its own workspaces and switches on its own.

Features:
• Separate workspaces (spaces) per monitor, each with its own count, remembered per screen
• A top bar with a workspace indicator on every monitor: scroll to switch, click a dot to go there, drag to reorder, right-click to remove, + to add
• Maximize or full-screen a window and it gets its own space, like the macOS green button; restore or close it to go back
• Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right, Super+Page Up/Down and the 3-finger touchpad swipe switch only the screen under the pointer
• Ctrl+Alt+= adds a space, Ctrl+Alt+- removes the current one
• Your workspace settings (dynamic workspaces, workspaces on primary only, number of workspaces) are restored when the extension is disabled

Great for multi-monitor setups: dual screen, laptop + external display, ultrawide + second screen.

Bugs and ideas: https://github.com/slim8/per-screen-workspaces/issues
